competences: The learner identifies key facts about the legislature.
The learner explains information about Parliament: duties, officers and qualifications of a Member of Parliament using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes legislature, parliament, speaker.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about the legislature.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Parliament: duties, officers and qualifications of a Member of Parliament.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about the legislature.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on Parliament: duties, officers and qualifications of a Member of Parliament
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces the legislature. They ask "What is legislature?" and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the legislature
steps.content: It is headed by the parliamentary speaker. People who belongs to the legislature To protect the national constitution Legislature is headed by the speaker of parliament. Important personalities in parliament. The legislature is headed by the speaker of the parliament. The speaker of the parliament The speaker is the chairperson of parliament. He alerts members of the parliament when the speaker is about to enter. A mace is a symbol of authority that represents the power of the speaker and parliament Qualifications for one to become a member of parliament The speaker of parliament Speaker of parliament
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the legislature on the chalkboard, including "It is headed by the parliamentary speaker. People who belongs to the legislature; To protect the national constitution Legislature is headed by the speaker of parliament. Important". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about the legislature
steps.content: Chairs parliamentary debates in the absence of the speaker. He/she alerts members of parliament when the speaker is about to enter Clerk to parliament Note: Roles of the speaker The speaker chairs parliamentary meetings The parliamentary speaker is assisted by the deputy speaker. He/ she chairs all the debates in parliament. The clerk to parliament He is the administrative head of parliament who keeps records and property of parliament. He acts as the secretary to the parliament.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the legislature on the chalkboard, including "Chairs parliamentary debates in the absence of the speaker.; He/she alerts members of parliament when the speaker is about to enter". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about the legislature
steps.content: He records all the parliamentary proceedings. (Hansard) He is in charge of security in the parliament. Legislature is the national assembly of a country. Legislature is the law-making body in Uganda. Before Uganda became independent, the assembly was called the legislature council He /she is the head of parliament He /she chairs parliamentary debates He/she presides over functions of parliament Clerk to parliament
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the legislature on the chalkboard, including "He records all the parliamentary proceedings. (Hansard); He is in charge of security in the parliament.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: What is legislature? | State one duty of the legislature arm of the government. | Who heads the legislature? | What title is given to the chief administrative head of the parliament? | Give the roles of the following officers in the parliament.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "What is legislature?" and "State one duty of the legislature arm of the government.". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on the legislature, asks "What is legislature?" and follows up with "State one duty of the legislature arm of the government.". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "What is legislature?" and "State one duty of the legislature arm of the government.", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Who was the first parliamentary speaker of Uganda?"
